summary:
LFM2.5-2.6B: 16 of 21 screens passed, all large units (1024–4096-unit MLP clusters or groups of 4–6 heads). Several passes only narrowly beat random same-size parts (most of the facts clusters, and the L9 month and L2 facts head groups), so treat those as weak.

**Head groups (the strongest results)**
- Capital city, L21 heads 3, 7, 10, 28: −.73 (random ≤ .04). Head 7 is the key; growing to 6 heads leaks into facts.
- Antonym, L21 heads 3, 10, 20, 27: −.39 (random ≤ .05). Head 20's static OV writes a word's antonym (z +5.8) and suppresses the word itself (z −7.5). 6-head versions reached −.47 to −.51 but leaked into facts and month.
- Past tense, L27 heads 17, 28, 30, 31: −.28 (random ≤ .04). A 6-head version adding heads 14 and 15 also passed at −.26. Static OV maps a base verb onto its irregular past form: head 28 z +13.3, 31 +6.1, 17 +4.7.
- Object colour, L17 heads 11, 14, 16, 19: −.30 (random ≤ .04). These are routers; their OV writes no colour tokens. A 6-head version adding the OV colour writers 17 and 21 also passed at −.24 (random ≤ .11).
- Month successor, L9 heads 13, 15, 30, 31: −.55 (weekday −.17). Random 4-head parts reached −.40, so the margin is modest.
- Facts, L2 heads 4, 6, 13, 14, 22, 25: −.84. Random 6-head parts reached −.61, so the margin is real but not large.

**MLP clusters**
- Facts, five clusters. Only L23 clears random clearly; the other four sit within about .03–.12 of their worst random part, L25 essentially at chance.
  - L3, 2048 units: −.46 (random up to −.34)
  - L23, 1024: −.44 (random ≤ −.12, the clearest)
  - L24, 2048: −.30 (random up to −.25)
  - L26, 4096: −.30 (random up to −.27)
  - L25, 2048: −.22 (random up to −.21)
- Roman numerals, L25, 1024: −.39 (random ≤ .02).
- Month successor, two clusters, each leaving weekday at about −.02/−.03:
  - L12, 2048: −.19 (random ≤ .09)
  - L13, 2048: −.21 (random ≤ .10)

**Failed screens**
- Month clusters at L9 (3072 units), L21 and L23 (2048 each) all failed the held-out check; at L9 random parts also dropped month more (.31 vs .18).
- L5 month heads 16, 17, 19, 28 and L13 month heads 3, 8, 19, 20 failed against random parts. In both layers a random same-size group often hits critical heads (L5 head 1; random L13 groups dropped month up to .76).

**Methods that worked**
- MLP clusters:
  1. Ablate each whole MLP to find layers that carry a skill.
  2. Take about 8 attribution seeds there; the scans only return about 20 units per layer.
  3. Add every unit whose gate (w1) row projects onto the seeds' gate-row span, minus 2–4x its projection onto the seed spans of leaking skills. A wider 48–64-unit basis from an already-screened cluster worked better for subtracting facts.
- Head groups: rank heads by static OV mapping (input token → target token, compared with the input itself), then trim by attribution and by swapping one head at a time. Head effects interact strongly, so check each subset by ablation.

**Leads that never passed**
- L9 facts heads 3, 17, 19, 20, 21, 29: clean but only .149.
- L24 weekday MLP cluster: .23, but facts leaks .17.
- L21 colour heads 0, 4, 15, 30: .23, but month leaks .10.
- L17 facts heads 4, 16, 20, 22: .31, but past tense and month leak.

**Negative results**
- No 1- or 2-layer block was selective.
- Nothing selective turned up for math or code. Math stayed within .12 for every whole MLP tested and is synergistic across attention.
- Ordinal word is robust (base .98).
- Multilingual never separated from facts or general_text.
- The agent skill cap was already reached, so I could not add arithmetic or translation tests.

summary: One new screened part: a 2048-unit L19 MLP family labelled past-tense verb inflection (catalog mlp_past-tense_verb_inflection_l19_mlp_family_2048_lfm2.5_2.6b_L19_k2048_001). It drops past_tense .248 (control +.003); every other skill moved under .04 and random parts dropped it at most .022. Recipe: past_tense attribution seeds L19 6016/5224/7020/1589, rank units by 0.5*cos(w1 row)+0.5*cos(w2 col) to the seeds, subtract the max score against month seeds (3640/4442/3004/4105) and weekday seeds. The drop grew with size: 256→.14, 512→.163, 1024→.185 (held-out failed), 2048→.248. Without the month penalty the family leaked month_successor .057-.074. Negatives: input-side embedding-projection clusters at L3 (weekday/past/ordinal, 512) dropped their targets under .05. Seeded families for colour (L22) peaked at .107 at 2048, antonym (L19) at .014 and month (L19) at .113 (1024 and 2048 the same), and code (L10) was broad (facts/general_text). Whole block L19 was nonselective. Head quads L17 [7,8,21,22] (weekday .257 but month .49, facts .24) and L13 [1,4,13,22] (code/multilingual attribution, broad damage) were too broad.

summary: LFM2.5-2.6B: two new large MLP parts passed. Both are L26 object_color families seeded from attribution unit 5781 (.087, almost twice the next unit), and grown by gate/up/down cosine to the seeds minus a capital-seed penalty. The 256-unit version dropped object_color .26 and the 1024-unit version .262. Other skills stayed ≤.048, controls ≤.004 and random parts ≤.02. Failures: L22 object_color families (256: .073 selective, 1024: .094, beaten by a random draw); L22 code family (.066, broad leaks to roman and facts); L24 object_color (.125, random hit .25); L27 capital family (broad); L25 capital (.047, selective but weak); L28 antonym family (.121, with object_color leaking .111). Lesson: on this model, a dominant attribution seed in late layers (L26) grows into clean families of 256-1024 units, while families from weak seeds stay below .13.
